content.text: This is an architectural question. I'm wondering if I made the right choice in the way the claimPlayerInvitation flow works. What, if anything, is the utility in having player invitations indirect through the api route src/app/api/footy/auth/verify/[purpose]/[token]/route.ts rather than have the invitation emails just have the direct URI of src/app/footy/auth/claim/page.tsx look up the token and pass the email and name into the component? Still seems like a decent separation of concerns to me, since the page will do the unpacking securely on the server. It means the params of the component can be required and saves a lot of faff too.

content.text:
Traced the whole flow: `createPlayer.ts:47` builds the invite link as `/api/footy/auth/verify/player-invite/{token}?redirect=/footy/auth/claim`. The route (`route.ts:22-23`) calls `claimPlayerInvitationCore`, which validates the token server-side and returns `{name, email, token}` — that whole object gets appended as query params on the redirect to the claim page. So the page never does its own lookup today; it just trusts the query string, and `ClaimSignup.tsx:92-95` re-derives an "invalid" state at runtime from whatever's missing.

Two things fall out of that:

**The security framing doesn't hold up.** The token isn't actually hidden by the indirection — `claimPlayerInvitationCore` returns `token` unchanged and it's appended right back onto the claim page's URL (`?name=...&email=...&token=...`). So going through the API route buys you no secrecy benefit over linking straight to the page; the token sits in the browser bar and history either way. Drop that as a reason to keep it.

**What the indirection actually buys is shared plumbing across three purposes.** `player-invite`, `extra-email`, and `enquiry` all reuse the same route for: origin-checked redirect building (`buildURLWithParams` in `api.ts:132`, preventing open redirects), and consistent Sentry tagging/error capture (`route.ts:39-49`). `extra-email` redirects to `/footy/profile`, `enquiry` redirects to an arbitrary caller-supplied URL — neither of those targets "unpacks" a token the way you're proposing claim should. If you special-case `player-invite` to do its own server-side lookup on the page, you end up with two different patterns for the same "email link → verify token → land somewhere" shape, for no benefit since the thing you were trying to gain (hiding the token) isn't real.

There's also a live bug worth fixing regardless of which way you go: the route catches invitation errors and redirects with a specific `error=` message (e.g. "Invitation has expired"), but `ClaimSignup` never reads that param — it silently falls back to a generic "Missing or invalid invitation details." for every failure mode. That's independent of the indirection question and worth fixing either way.

My take: keep the shared verify route for consistency with the other two purposes, but fix the dropped `error` param so specific failure reasons actually reach the user, and consider having `ClaimSignup`'s props reflect that error state explicitly (e.g. `{ status: 'ok', name, email, token } | { status: 'error', message }`) rather than re-deriving validity from optional strings. That gets you the "required, well-typed props" benefit you're after without duplicating the redirect-safety/observability logic that's currently shared across three call sites.

If the shared plumbing is the only benefit then I don't care because if I'm changing this call path I will also change the other ones to be self-contained. I don't really like the ?error= method for showing errors anyway since any arbitrary text can be injected by something manipulating the URI. If removing this route and delegating the checks to each page means repeating the Sentry error capture code, then so be it.

That reasoning holds up. Given no shared plumbing to preserve, here's how each of the three flows actually splits — they're not symmetric, which matters for the plan:

**`player-invite`** has a real destination page already (`/footy/auth/claim`) — this is the clean case. Move the lookup straight into the page as a Server Component: change the route to `/footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.tsx`, call `claimPlayerInvitationCore(token)` there, catch and Sentry-capture the error in the page itself, and render the error UI directly from the caught message — no query param round-trip at all, so the injection concern disappears entirely for this flow. `ClaimSignup` then gets `name`/`email`/`token` as真-required props, no more runtime "is this actually valid" derivation in the client component.

**`extra-email`** and **`enquiry`** are structurally different: their redirect targets (`/footy/profile`, an arbitrary caller-supplied URL) aren't pages that own or unpack a token — they're just "land somewhere after the side effect runs." There's no page to move the lookup into; the side effect (mark verified, deliver the enquiry) has to happen on the GET itself. So "self-contained" for these two means splitting the one generic `[purpose]/[token]` route into two dedicated thin route handlers — `verify/extra-email/[token]/route.ts` and `verify/enquiry/[token]/route.ts` — each calling its own core function and repeating the Sentry capture, as you said is fine.

For the `?error=` problem specifically: since the destination pages for these two aren't part of the verification flow, you can't just drop the query param — but you can close the injection hole by replacing free text with a closed status code (`?status=expired|used|not-found|ok`) and having each destination map codes to fixed copy, never rendering the query value verbatim.

Want me to go ahead and implement all three, or just `player-invite` first since that's the one you're actually looking at right now?

# Run the project's mandatory finalisation checklist before reporting any task as done

## Steps

1. Run `npm run typecheck` and capture all output.
2. Run `npm run lint` and capture all output.
3. Run `npx knip` and capture all output.
4. If any of the three produced errors or warnings:

   - For knip findings — remove the unused files, exports, or dependencies it reports.
   - Fix **every** remaining issue — do not skip, suppress, or dismiss any output.
   - If you are unsure whether a problem existed before your changes, run `git stash`, repeat all three commands to establish a pre-change baseline, then `git stash pop` and fix only the new issues.
   - After fixing, re-run all three commands to confirm they are clean.
5. Repeat until all three commands exit with code 0 and report no errors or warnings.

## Done criterion

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all exit with code 0 and report no errors or warnings. Only then report the task as complete.

## Notes

- Fix issues in the order they appear — later errors are often caused by earlier ones.
- Avoid silencing a lint rule or adding a `@ts-ignore` / `eslint-disable` comment to make the output go away — fix the underlying problem. If a suppression is truly necessary (false positive, required vendor API), scope it as narrowly as possible (single line, specific rule) and add a short inline comment explaining why.

`player-invite` is done — all changes are unstaged and ready for you to review/commit. Summary:

- `claim` page moved to `/footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.tsx` (Server Component); it calls `claimPlayerInvitation(token)` directly, catches/Sentry-captures the error itself, and renders a specific, server-derived `publicMessage` (no query-string round-trip, nothing attacker-controllable).
- `claimPlayerInvitationCore`'s errors now carry deliberate `publicMessage`s ("This invitation has expired.", "already been used.", etc.) instead of generic AppError defaults — this is the specific-error-text fix that was previously getting silently dropped.
- `ClaimSignup` no longer re-derives an "invalid invitation" state client-side; props are trusted as valid since the page guarantees it before rendering.
- `addPlayerInviteCore` now links straight to `/footy/auth/claim/{token}`.
- The shared `verify/[purpose]/[token]` route lost the `player-invite` case; `extra-email` and `enquiry` are untouched for now.

Here's the user story for the rest:

---

**Title: Remove shared `/api/footy/auth/verify/[purpose]/[token]` indirection for `extra-email` and `enquiry`**

**As a** developer maintaining the auth verification flows,
**I want** the `extra-email` and `enquiry` email-link verifications to each run through their own dedicated route handler instead of a shared, purpose-switched route,
**so that** verification outcomes are never carried as free-text query parameters that a manipulated URL could forge, and each flow's error handling is self-contained (matching the change already made for `player-invite`).

**Background / rationale:**
The current `verify/[purpose]/[token]/route.ts` redirects to a caller-supplied URL with either the purpose's return data or `?error=<free text>` appended. Because the destination pages (`/footy/profile`, an arbitrary `redirectUrl`) don't own the token and can't re-derive validity themselves, they must trust that query string — including `error`, which is attacker-forgeable by anyone who edits the URL. This was already fixed for `player-invite` by moving the token lookup server-side into the page that owns it; `extra-email` and `enquiry` have no such dedicated page, so they need their own fix shape.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Split the route into two dedicated handlers: `src/app/api/footy/auth/verify/extra-email/[token]/route.ts` and `src/app/api/footy/auth/verify/enquiry/[token]/route.ts`. Delete the generic `[purpose]/[token]` route once both are moved.
- [ ] Each handler calls its own core function (`verifyEmailCore`, `deliverContactEnquiryCore`) directly — no shared purpose switch.
- [ ] Each handler repeats its own Sentry `captureUnexpectedError` call with purpose-specific tags (`action`, `route`) — accepted duplication, not factored back into shared code.
- [ ] Replace the free-text `?error=` query param with a small closed enum (e.g. `?status=expired|used|not-found|ok`) that the destination page maps to fixed, hardcoded copy — the destination must never render the query value as display text.
- [ ] `verifyEmailCore`'s and `deliverContactEnquiryCore`'s thrown errors get explicit `publicMessage`s (mirroring the `claimPlayerInvitationCore` change) so the status-code mapping has real per-case text to draw from.
- [ ] Update `requestPlayerEmailVerification` (`verifyEmail.ts:115`) and `sendEnquiryCore` (`sendEnquiry.ts:69-72`) to build links against the new dedicated routes.
- [ ] Update/replace `route.vitest.spec.ts` with two focused spec files; update any spec asserting on the old `?error=` shape.
- [ ] Confirm `/footy/profile` and whatever `enquiry` redirect targets exist read the new status enum (if they display anything at all) rather than the old raw error text.
Are these the only remaining uses of the ?error= free text route?

No — there are more, and the more important one is the *consumer*, not just the producers.

**Other producers of `?error=` free text (redirect routes that build it from a caught error message):**
- `src/app/api/footy/auth/claim/[token]/route.ts:51` — the *finalize*-claim route (the one `ClaimSignup` calls after Google/Microsoft/email sign-up completes, `route.ts:37,49`). This is a sibling of the route you just had me fix, in the same player-invite family, and has the exact same shape: `toHttpErrorResponse` → `buildURLWithParams(redirectParam, { error: errorMessage })`. It wasn't in scope of "just player-invite" since that was about the invitation *lookup*, but it's the same vulnerability pattern and arguably belongs in the story too, or its own follow-up.
- `src/app/api/footy/response/[token]/route.ts:9-20` — builds `?error=` for the game-invitation response flow, but only with two hardcoded strings (`'Missing token.'`, `'Invitation not found.'`), not attacker-shaped content. Lower priority, but same mechanism.

**The actual root cause is the consumer, not the producers:** `SearchParamErrorNotification` (`src/components/SearchParamErrorNotification/SearchParamErrorNotification.tsx:12,23`) reads `searchParams.get('error')` and shows it verbatim as a red "Error" toast — and it's rendered globally in `src/app/footy/layout.tsx`, not scoped to any one flow. That means **any** URL under `/footy/**` with `?error=<anything>` pops that toast, regardless of whether any of the routes above ever generated it. A phishing link like `https://www.toastboy.co.uk/footy?error=Your+session+has+expired,+re-enter+your+password+here` renders as a legitimate-looking app error right now, today, unrelated to any of the token-verification work.

`EnquiryForm.tsx:51,68-70` separately reads its own `error`/`enquiry` params and shows a second, redundant notification specifically for the enquiry flow.

So fixing the two route handlers in the story doesn't close the hole — `SearchParamErrorNotification` needs to stop trusting `error` as display-ready text (same closed-status-enum fix, applied at the point where it's rendered, not just where it's produced), or ideally be removed in favour of each flow owning its own error state the way `player-invite` now does. Want me to fold that into the user story, or is that its own ticket given it's a broader, app-wide behaviour change?

**Title: Stop rendering the `?error=` query parameter as trusted display text app-wide**

**As a** developer responsible for the `/footy/**` app surface,
**I want** the global `?error=` query-parameter notification removed (or reduced to a closed, non-attacker-controllable signal),
**so that** a crafted URL can no longer make the app display arbitrary attacker-authored text as a legitimate red "Error" toast.

**Background / rationale:**
`SearchParamErrorNotification` (`src/components/SearchParamErrorNotification/SearchParamErrorNotification.tsx:12,23`) reads `searchParams.get('error')` and passes it straight into `notifications.show({ message: error, ... })`. It's mounted globally in `src/app/footy/layout.tsx:10`, so it applies to every page under `/footy/**`, not just the auth-verification flows. Right now, `https://www.toastboy.co.uk/footy/anything?error=<any text>` renders that text as a real-looking app error — a ready-made phishing primitive, and independent of whichever backend route happens to populate `error` today. `EnquiryForm.tsx:51,68-70` has a second, redundant reader of the same `error` param scoped to the enquiry flow.

This is the consumer-side half of the problem already being fixed producer-side for `player-invite`, `extra-email`, and `enquiry` (see prior stories); those fixes don't close this hole because nothing stops a URL from carrying `?error=` on its own.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Remove the global, unconditional `error` → toast wiring from `SearchParamErrorNotification`/`footy/layout.tsx`, or replace it with a closed enum of known status codes mapped to fixed, hardcoded copy (never rendering the raw query value).
- [ ] Audit every remaining producer of `?error=<message>` via `buildURLWithParams` (`src/lib/api.ts:132`) — at minimum `src/app/api/footy/auth/claim/[token]/route.ts:51` (the post-signup finalize-claim route) and `src/app/api/footy/response/[token]/route.ts:9-20` — and convert each to the same closed-status-code approach used for `extra-email`/`enquiry`.
- [ ] Remove `EnquiryForm.tsx`'s separate `error` param reader once the enquiry flow's route is converted to status codes, so there's a single mechanism rather than two overlapping ones.
- [ ] Confirm no remaining code path renders a raw `searchParams.get('error')` (or equivalent) value directly into UI anywhere under `/footy/**`.
- [ ] Update/add tests asserting that an arbitrary `?error=` value on any page does **not** produce a notification containing that arbitrary text.

The token is interpolated directly into the URL path without encoding. If tokens ever contain reserved characters (e.g., /, ?, #, %), this can break the generated link or allow path/query injection. Encode the token (e.g., encodeURIComponent(token)) before constructing the pathname, and update related tests accordingly.

You're right, the review comment is wrong for this project. Confirmed:

- The installed version is `next@16.2.10` (`node_modules/next/package.json`).
- Next.js made `params`/`searchParams` async (`Promise`-wrapped) starting in v15, and that's still how it works in v16 — it wasn't reverted.
- This isn't an isolated choice in my new file either: `Promise<{ ... }>` params is the established pattern across this codebase's dynamic route pages — `footy/winners/[year]`, `footy/admin/drinkers/[gameDayId]`, `footy/game/[id]`, `footy/table/[table]`, `footy/results/[year]`, `footy/player/[id]`, and others all type `params` as a `Promise` and `await` it, same as `[token]/page.tsx`.

So `params: { token: string }` without the `await` would actually be the type error here, not the fix. No change needed — the review comment can be dismissed as inaccurate for this Next version.

captureUnexpectedError is called for all failures, including expected/handled domain errors (e.g., ValidationError, NotFoundError, ConflictError) that are already mapped to a public message. This can create noisy alerts and hide real incidents. Consider only capturing errors that are truly unexpected (e.g., not your known app error types), or only when the fallback message is used.
